newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end lower on registrations, weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end lower on registrations, weather.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended lower on Thursday with nearbys down on news 50,000 bushels of soybeans were registered for delivery, traders said.

Trade sources had anticipated registrations but many were surprised the soybeans were posted in St. Louis rather than Chicago. There had been widespread rumors in recent weeks that a commercial firm was bringing soybeans into Chicago.
New crop months crumbled amid weather forecasts for widespread rains across parched portions of Illinois.

"Weather continues to be the dominant feature out here," said Mark Weidner, analyst with Cargill Investor Services. "The majority of the trade's belief is that next week's system is going to be able to tap into the Gulf moisture."
Weather Express Chief Forecaster Fred Gesser said moisture from Tropical Storm Danny would move north, soaking Illinois. Recent rains bypassed central Illinois.

"Moisture from what should become Tropical Storm Danny is in a position to provide 0.50 to 2.00-plus inches with 80 percent coverage for Missouri and southern Illinois up to Peoria on Monday," Gesser said.
Soybeans ended down 9-1/4 to 7-1/4 cents per bushel with July off 7-1/2 at $7.74-1/2.

Old crop/new crop spreads firmed slightly in reaction to strength in the U.S. Gulf CIF market, floor sources said. Cash traders said river bids were higher while inland values fell as processors pulled back.

"We did have a little bit of a bounce in the old crop/new crop spreads, probably associated with some firmness in the CIF values," Weidner said. "We saw some sales in this morning's (USDA) report but we still need to get this stuff shipped."
USDA early Thursday put old crop soybean net export sales at 117,500 tonnes.
The trade had expected between 100,000 to 150,000 tonnes.
New crop sales of 528,300 tonnes were above expectations for 250,000 to 450,000 tonnes.
Gains in old crop months were limited by expectations for a low weekly crush figure. The National Oilseed Processors Association will release its weekly crush data early Friday.
Trade sources expected it to show between 21.5 and 22.8 million bushels of soybeans crushed, compared with 23 million the previous week.

On the day, commercials were buyers of the August. ADM bought three million August and Produce Grain bought 1.5 million August. Refco Inc and Dean Witter each bought 2.5 million November, traders said.
Lind-Waldock was a featured seller on the day, accounting for at least three million bushels sold in the November. Tenco Inc sold 1.5 million August.
In options trade, ADM bought 500 September $6.75 calls and sold 500 September $7.00 calls at 5-3/4 cents. Lind-Waldock bought 500 November $6.00 puts and sold 500 November $5.75 puts at 11-1/4 cents.
Volatility in the August was pegged at 31 percent, down sharply from Wednesday's 45-1/2. Volatility in the November was at 23-1/2, down from 33 percent on Wednesday.
Soybean futures volume was pegged at 52,000 contracts, compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 52,160. Options volume was estimated at 26,000 contracts, against Wednesday's 28,087 contracts.
